Here is a recap of what happened in the search forums today, through the eyes of the Search Engine Roundtable and other search forums on the web.
The FBI posted an alert about SEO poisoning through malware. Moving a site does not and should not improve a site's quality, according to Google. Google is testing sign-in CAPTCHAs after the first query, it seems. Google explained a couple reasons why it is bad to serve a 200 status code when your site is down. Google has a new Google-Agent bot help document. Google Business Profiles added an option to add your Facebook Messenger account to your Google listing. You can now download your Google Local Service Ads historical reporting. Google Ads posted a new help document named About Search Journey Awareness. Google Ads added a new option under the brand guidelines for Performance Max campaigns to add visual guidelines.
Search Engine Roundtable Stories:
-
FBI: SEO Poisoning Led To $28 Million In Ransomware Payments
The FBI, Federal Bureau of Investigation, has a newsletter named the FBI FLASH, and in the November 16th edition, it highlighted SEO poisoning through Gootloader malware. This resulted in "over 1000 infected WordPress sites and 216 domains controlled by the Gootloader administrator, which led to over $28 million in ransomware payments," the FBI said. -
Google: A Site Move Doesn't Improve A Site's Overall Quality
John Mueller from Google said that simply moving a site to a new domain does not improve a site's overall quality. He wrote this on Bluesky, "A site move doesn't improve the site's overall quality." I mean, this is pretty obvious, but sometimes I like to cover the obvious. -
Google Tests Sign In Protections After First Search To Block Scrapers
Google has been testing numerous ways to block scrapers and third-party tools from crawling its search results page. The latest effort seems to require a user to sign in immediately after the first search. But Rajan Patel from Google said on X that he will look into this but "I don't believe it's meant to happen on the first page of results like this but we may be testing something here..." -
Google On Why Serving A 200 Status Code When Your Site Is Down Is Bad
Google's John Mueller posted two reasons why it would be bad to serve a 200 status code to Googlebot when your site or web pages are down. He said that if your site is down and the page says an error message, that message will be shown in the Google Search results and also, if the same text is on all your pages, Google can de-duplicate the pages and your pages can drop out of the index. -
New Google Search Help Document On How To Allow Google-Agent Traffic
Google released a new help document on how to allow Google-Agent to have access to your website. "Google-Agent is the name used by agents hosted on Google infrastructure to navigate the web and perform actions upon user request," the document says. -
Google Business Profiles Now Lets You Add Facebook Messenger Number
Google Business Profiles added an option to add your Facebook Messenger account to your Google listing. Google recently sent out emails about this, where they added it automatically for you, but now it lets you manually add it when you edit your profile. -
Google Local Services Ads Historical Reports Can Now Be Downloaded
You can now download your historical Google Local Services Ads reports on the redirection page of Google Local Services Ads. Previously, Google said the download feature was coming and now Google said it is finally here. -
New Google Ads Search Journey Awareness Help Document
Google Ads posted a new help document named About Search Journey Awareness. Journey-Aware Bidding is not new, but I believe this help document is new. Google explained, "Search Journey Awareness is an improvement to Google Ads Smart Bidding." -
Google Ads Brand Guidelines New Add Visual Guidelines
Google Ads added a new option under the brand guidelines for Performance Max campaigns to add visual guidelines. This says, "Now you can add style references and preferences to help steer how images are created and enhanced for your ads." -
Android Table Model Of London
Here is a photo from the Android Dev Summit in London that shows this table with the Android logo and then like an Android town in London.
